sections.subtitle: Current Form
sections.text: Liverpool are in strong form, having won three of their last five matches, including impressive clean-sheet victories. West Ham United, on the other hand, have shown resilience with no losses in their last four games, though they’ve struggled to convert chances into decisive wins. This contrast suggests Liverpool hold the edge going into this clash at Anfield.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-Head Record
sections.text: Recent encounters heavily favor Liverpool, who have won four of the last five matchups against West Ham, including both of the last two head-to-heads. West Ham have consistently failed to keep a clean sheet against Liverpool in their last 20 meetings, which could spell trouble for the visitors today.

sections.subtitle: Key Players to Watch
sections.text: For Liverpool, players like Dominik Szoboszlai and Mohamed Salah have been in fine form, contributing significantly in recent games. West Ham will rely on Jarrod Bowen and Crysencio Summerville to exploit any defensive lapses, with their attacking output crucial for an upset.

sections.subtitle: Tactical Insights
sections.text: Liverpool’s high possession game and ability to create big chances could dominate West Ham, who often struggle against top sides. West Ham’s recent defensive solidity might help them stay competitive, but their lower conversion rate could hinder their chances of a positive result.

sections.subtitle: Statistical Edge
sections.text: Liverpool rank higher in key areas like ball possession and penalty area entries, reflecting their attacking intent. West Ham, sitting lower in the league table, have conceded more goals this season, which aligns with their historical defensive struggles against Liverpool.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Half-time overview
halftimeSections.text: At half-time, Liverpool lead West Ham United by a commanding 3-0 scoreline at Anfield. The home side has dominated much of the first half, capitalizing on their chances with clinical finishing. Goals from Hugo Ekitiké, Virgil van Dijk, and Alexis Mac Allister have put Liverpool in a strong position. West Ham, despite showing some resilience, have struggled to convert their opportunities into goals, leaving them with a steep hill to climb in the second half.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Liverpool's dominance
halftimeSections.text: Liverpool have showcased their attacking prowess in the first half, with a significant edge in penalty area entries and corner kicks. Their ability to create dangerous moments in the final third has been evident, and they’ve been rewarded with three well-taken goals. Key players like Hugo Ekitiké, who scored early and contributed with an assist, and Alexis Mac Allister, with a goal of his own, have been instrumental. The Reds have also maintained a balanced possession share, allowing them to dictate the tempo for large spells of the game.

halftimeSections.subtitle: West Ham's struggles
halftimeSections.text: West Ham United have had their moments, particularly in the final third with a reasonable number of entries, but their finishing has let them down. Despite nearly matching Liverpool in possession, they’ve only managed a single shot on target, which highlights their lack of cutting edge in attack. Defensively, they’ve been exposed at crucial moments, conceding three goals from varied situations. Their physicality in duels and aerial challenges has been a positive, but it hasn’t translated into tangible results on the scoreboard.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum analysis
halftimeSections.text: The first half saw Liverpool start with a strong attacking intent, pushing forward with consistent pressure in the opening minutes and securing an early lead. Their momentum remained high during key spells, especially around the times of their second and third goals, where they overwhelmed West Ham's defense. West Ham, on the other hand, showed sporadic bursts of attacking intent, particularly in a few stretches in the middle of the half, but their efforts faded without significant threat. Towards the end of the half, Liverpool regained control with renewed attacking vigor, underlining their superiority.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key players to watch
halftimeSections.text: For Liverpool, Hugo Ekitiké has been the standout performer with a goal and an assist, showing sharpness in the final third. Mohamed Salah, while yet to score, remains a constant threat and could be pivotal in the second half. On West Ham’s side, Jarrod Bowen has shown flashes of creativity with key passes and could be the spark they need to get back into the game. Konstantinos Mavropanos has also been solid defensively despite the scoreline, and his contributions could be crucial if West Ham are to mount a comeback.
